title: Rooms for Gathering
subject: world-religions

introduction: Buildings where communities meet, and the names for the parts inside them.

entries.explanation: Sikh communities serve a shared vegetarian meal to anyone who comes, seated together on the floor.

factCards.text: Sikh gurdwaras serve langar, a free communal meal, to visitors of any background; the practice is attributed to Guru Nanak and formalised by later Gurus.

The mihrab appears in mosque architecture from the early eighth century CE; the Prophet's Mosque in Medina is often named as the setting of the first concave example, though the attribution is debated among architectural historians.
factCards.sourceTitle: Grove Encyclopedia of Islamic Art and Architecture — Mihrab

factCards.text: A torii marks the boundary of a Shinto shrine precinct, separating the everyday ground outside from the shrine ground within.
